Incident.Summary: The 23:00 night task failed while the release gate owned the hardware worker; the GUI restarted later, applied the saved day policy, and the actual limits stayed at 10 W from the gate test. A recovery helper call then clicked a hidden POLICY_SAVE control and left enabled=false.

RootCauses: Night task ran while the release gate had stopped the stable GUI/worker, so the helper could not reach the pipe.
The recovery helper clicked POLICY_SAVE even when the policy controls were hidden, saving stale in-memory toggles and disabling the automatic policy.
When the GUI restarted, it re-applied the saved day policy; the worker policy controller caches last_applied_target and does not re-verify actual limits after an external/firmware reset.
Fixes: Ensure-GuiWorker auto-start is now opt-in via -AllowGuiAutoStart; release gates and manual runs cannot spawn a second hardware owner.
Hidden policy controls are detected with IsWindowVisible before any save; simple/tray mode never posts POLICY_SAVE.
Hidden-control paths can reload the saved policy by gracefully restarting the tray GUI via -RefreshGui.
The PASS log now records gui=in-place|restarted|deferred|skipped instead of a boolean guiSynced state.

Regressions.AutoStartRefusalWithoutSwitch: PASS (worker pipe unavailable and GUI auto-start is disabled for this call)
Regressions.AutoStartWithSwitch: PASS (STARTED GUI, then RESTARTED GUI to reload the saved policy)

ResidualRisk: The packaged 1.0.40 worker still re-applies only after a power-line change or task run; a firmware/EC reset can drift limits until the next event. A limits-aware re-assert is the next source candidate.
